Lei Feng exclusively learned that embodied intelligence startup AtomBite.AI has recently completed a multi-million yuan seed round of financing. This round was led by Inno Science and Technology Innovation Fund, with follow-on investments from Tsinghua SEM Alumni Seed Fund and well-known individual investors. Dr. Wang Dong, founder and CEO of AtomBite.AI, studied under China's AI pioneer, Academician Zhang Bo of Tsinghua University. With over a decade of experience in AI, he combines algorithm research with commercial application expertise.

Academically, Dr. Wang focused on AI representation issues during his PhD and consistently published high-level papers at top AI and robotics conferences. In 2011, he built the world's first commercial video facial recognition and tracking system. Later, he developed industry-leading local life service recommendation systems and mobile native advertising platforms, deeply integrating cutting-edge AI technology with complex commercial scenarios.

Co-founder Li Tao previously led Meituan's food delivery algorithm and data systems.

items.title: 寻找 AI 的「第三语言」：中间表示如何打通多模态鸿沟 ｜ CVPR 2026
items.raw_excerpt: “请把杯子拿起来”。 这句话对你来说轻而易举。因为你看到了杯子，理解了“拿起来”的含义，手自然地伸过去、捏住、提起。但对一个 AI 系统来说，这中间隔着数道几乎不可逾越的鸿沟：语言到动作、动作到视觉、视觉到空间、空间到执行。 传统做法是强迫模型学会直接映射，通过输入一段文字或一组动作参数，让其直接输出像素级的视频帧或关节角度。这种方法在受限环境和充足标注数据下勉强可行，但一旦面对真实世界的复杂性，系统就会崩溃，因为鸿沟太宽，直接跨越注定失败。 清华大学智能产业研究院赵昊团队在 CVPR 2026 发表的四篇论文，共享着同一个设计哲学： 当两种模态之间的鸿沟太大，真正的解法是为它们搭桥，找到一种“第三语言”。这个“第三语言”，就是中间表示。 这四篇论文分别从动作到视频、图像到 4D 场景、首帧到未来视频、异构硬件到统一策略四个不同的角度，验证了同一个核心假设： 引入合适的中间表示，比强迫模型学会直接映射更有效。 01 ORV： 当机器人看视频时，它在看什么？ 机器人学习领域有一个看似简单却长期未能很好解决的问题：如何让机器人通过观看人类操作视频来学习新技能？ 这个问题的困难程度远超想象。对人类来说直观的东西，对机器人来说却是无法理解的数据流，因为视频是一帧帧像素，动作是七维或更高维的连续控制信号，这两种表示之间存在巨大的“表征鸿沟”。 现有的机器人视频生成方法通常采用端到端的方式：输入动作序列，直接输出对应的视频帧。这种做法在实践中面临两个根本性问题： 动作空间和像素空间的结构差异太大， 动作是低维的连续向量，像素是高维的离散网格，强行让模型学习从前者到后者的直接映射，就像让一个只会说中文的人直接听懂法语，中间没有任何翻译。 缺乏结构化约束 ：生成的视频往往在多视角一致性上表现糟糕。同一个动作从两个不同视角看，本应是同一个 3D 事件的不同投影，但端到端模型经常会生成两个视角

excerpt_i18n.en: "Please pick up the cup." This sentence is effortless for you. You see the cup, understand the meaning of "pick up," and your hand naturally reaches out, grasps, and lifts it. But for an AI system, this involves several nearly insurmountable gaps: from language to action, action to vision, vision to space, and space to execution. The traditional approach forces the model to learn direct mapping by inputting a piece of text or a set of action parameters, directly outputting pixel-level video frames or joint angles. This method barely works in constrained environments with sufficient annotated data, but once faced with the complexity of the real world, the system collapses because the gaps are too wide, and direct bridging is doomed to fail. The four papers published by Zhao Hao's team from the Institute for AI Industry Research (AIR) at Tsinghua University at CVPR 2026 share the same design philosophy: when the gap between two modalities is too large, the real solution is to build a bridge for them, finding a "third language." This "third language" is the intermediate representation. These four papers validate the same core hypothesis from four different perspectives—action to video, image to 4D scene, first frame to future video, and heterogeneous hardware to unified strategy: introducing an appropriate intermediate representation is more effective than forcing the model to learn direct mapping. 01 ORV: When a robot watches a video, what does it see? In the field of robot learning, there is a seemingly simple yet long-unresolved problem: how to enable robots to learn new skills by watching videos of human operations? The difficulty of this problem far exceeds imagination.
excerpt_i18n.es: "Por favor, levanta la taza". Esta frase te resulta sencilla. Porque ves la taza, entiendes el significado de "levantar", y tu mano se extiende de forma natural, la agarra y la eleva. Pero para un sistema de IA, entre medias hay varias brechas casi insalvables: del lenguaje a la acción, de la acción a la visión, de la visión al espacio, del espacio a la ejecución. El enfoque tradicional obliga al modelo a aprender un mapeo directo, introduciendo un texto o un conjunto de parámetros de acción para que genere directamente fotogramas a nivel de píxel o ángulos articulares. Este método funciona a duras penas en entornos controlados y con datos etiquetados suficientes, pero al enfrentarse a la complejidad del mundo real, el sistema colapsa, porque la brecha es demasiado amplia y cruzarla directamente está condenado al fracaso.

excerpt_i18n.en: Google I/O has always been the most information-dense node on the global developer calendar and the ultimate stage for tech giants to showcase their AI ambitions. On May 19, 2026, in Mountain View, California, Sundar Pichai unveiled 16 core product updates in two hours. Among them, five products each boast 3 billion users, the Gemini assistant has 900 million users, and Search AI Mode, launched just a year ago, has surpassed 1 billion monthly active users. There was no suspenseful "One More Thing" rhythm, no deliberately saved blockbuster finale. Google opted for a near-bombardment information release strategy: laying everything out on the table at once. Pichai made a thought-provoking remark on stage: "The most cutting-edge agents may have only reached 0.1% of the world's population. The real question is how to scale this frontier capability to truly broader users." The subtext was clear: agents today are still toys for a niche group of geeks and high-end enterprises, but Google aims to turn them into a daily reality for 3 billion people. excerpt_i18n.es: Google I/O siempre ha sido el punto de información más denso en el calendario global de desarrolladores, y también el escenario máximo donde los gigantes tecnológicos proclaman sus ambiciones en IA. El 19 de mayo de 2026, en Mountain View, California, Sundar Pichai lanzó 16 actualizaciones de productos principales en dos horas. Entre ellos, cinco productos cuentan cada uno con 3 mil millones de usuarios, el asistente Gemini tiene 900 millones de usuarios, y el modo AI de búsqueda, lanzado hace solo un año, superó los mil millones de usuarios activos mensuales. Sin el ritmo de suspense de "One More Thing", sin un huevo de pascua importante guardado para el final, Google optó por un enfoque casi de bombardeo.
